question: A shopkeeper was offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on an item whose marked price is ₹1,000, while another shopkeeper was offering a flat 33% discount on the same item. Find the positive difference in the nominal amounts of discounts given by the two shopkeepers on the sale of the item.
solution:
**Given:** 

The shopkeeper was offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on an item whose marked price is ₹1,000

Another shopkeeper was offering a flat 33% discount on the same item

**Formula Used: **

Successive Discount = X + Y - (XY)/(100)

**Calculation:**

On offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15%,

⇒ The single discount will be =X + Y - (XY)/(100)=20 + 15 - (20times 15)/(100)=35-(300)/(100)=35-3=32

The single discount will be 32%

⇒ The price of the item after the discount will be = MarkedPricetimes (discount)/(100)=1000times (32)/(100) =₹ 320

On offering the discount of 33% 

⇒ The price of the item after the discount will be = MarkedPricetimes (discount)/(100)= 1000times(33)/(100)=₹ 330

**Hence, The positive difference in the nominal amounts of discounts given by the two ****shopkeepers on the sale of the item will be = the price of the item after discount 33% - the price of the item after two successive discounts of 20% and 15%,**

**= ₹ 330 - ₹ 320**

**= ₹ 10 **
